title: Role of Interfacial Coherency on Creep Behavior of FCC/BCC High-Entropy Alloy Multilayers.

recollection.starting_material: guess: high-entropy alloy multilayers with FCC and BCC phases
recollection.intervention: guess: varying the interfacial coherency between the FCC and BCC layers
recollection.structure: guess: layered structure with varying degrees of interfacial coherency
recollection.mechanism: guess: dislocation movement and grain boundary sliding affected by interfacial coherency
recollection.results: guess: improved creep resistance with optimized interfacial coherency

score.note: The recollection only generically infers that interfacial coherency was varied in FCC/BCC multilayers. It does not identify the 8–80 nm modulation periods, coherent/semicoherent/grain-boundary regimes, the special role of M16 and misfit dislocations, or the proposed interfacial-amorphization/diffusion mechanism. No numerical creep results or stress exponents are recalled.
